## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown wings with dark speckling and wavy crosslines that help it blend into bark, dead leaves, and tree trunks. In Florida, it is found in oak hammocks, pine-oak woodlands, forest edges, parks, yards, and other wooded habitats where oaks are present. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on oak leaves and help move oak foliage into the broader food web as prey for birds, spiders, wasps, and other insect-eating animals.
